No, a court will likely not enforce the bar against assigning the right to payment. A general prohibition on assignment doesn't reach the right to receive the funds unless the contract specifically says it does. UCC § 2-210(2) allows assignment of a right arising from the seller's due performance of its entire obligation despite a contrary agreement, and UCC § 9-406(d) overrides contract terms that bar assigning a right to payment.

CONFIDENCE: 88
